title: GPU capacity tradeoffs + derivative scale-trigger notes
content:
Purpose: capture the informal results and heuristics from the June sim runs that evaluated a new scaling signal (utilization derivative / ramp-rate) combined with an explicit minimum cold-buffer per region. This doc is a working sheet for tuning min/max and trigger logic before we formalize into a runbook.

Summary finding (short): adding a derivative term to the scale-up trigger reduced overshoot for short spikes and allowed us to safely lower global min headroom by ~8% without visibility regressions in latency p95. However, derivative-only tuning struggles with sustained step increases (10m+), so we pair it with a slower-window utilization average for sustained decisions.

Quick TL;DR numbers (sim cohort average across 4 workload traces):
- baseline (current policy): target util 70%, min/global headroom 18%, p95 latency breaches noted during burst windows (3 of 8 traces)
- candidate A (util + derivative): derivative alpha=0.6, short-window 30s, long-window 5m -> allowed min headroom drop to 10% while keeping p95 within SLO for 6/8 traces
- candidate B (derivative + cooldown): same as A but 90s cooldown after scale-down -> smoother tail behavior, reduced oscillation count by ~40%

Per-region observed tradeoffs (notes, not canonical):
- us-west-2: bursty traffic, high variance; derivative triggers helped, suggested min-headroom 12% (lowered from 20%) with a cap on single-step scale percent at 25% to avoid huge one-shot provision ops.
- eu-west-1: steadier patterns, can tolerate lower min (8%) if we bias long-window average more strongly (5m weight=0.7).
- ap-southeast-1: cold-start risk high (spot preemption + longer cold startup); keep min at 18% and prefer slower ramp (scale-up threshold conservative) until we reduce cold-start time below 45s.

Sim sketch table (representative numbers):
region | baseline_min | candidateA_min | p95_breaches_baseline/8 | p95_breaches_A/8 | notes
us-west-2 | 20% | 12% | 3 | 1 | cap single-step at 25%
eu-west-1 | 14% | 8% | 1 | 0 | bias long-window
ap-southeast-1 | 22% | 18% | 4 | 3 | keep conservative until cold-start fix

Key heuristics to codify into policy: 
1) Two-signal decision model: short-window derivative for quick scale-ups, long-window moving-util for durability. Require both to indicate need for scale-down to reduce premature shrinkage.
2) Max single-step scale limit per region (configurable by region class) to avoid capacity churn when large traces arrive.
3) Cooldown windows asymmetric: short cooldown for scale-up (~30-90s depending on model size), longer for scale-down (3-8 minutes).
4) Cold-start budget: explicit per-region reserve (not counted towards autoscale) for markets with high preemption risk or long warm times.
5) Score decay: derivative signal should decay with recent successful scale-ups to avoid repeated triggers on same spike.

Open questions / caveats: 
- How to choose derivative alpha and safe single-step limit per region automatically? Need a small ML model or offline tuning loop that maps observed variance metrics to policy parameters.
- Interactions with KV cache effects: when cache hit-rate changes with model version, util signals shift; we must co-evaluate for rollout windows.
- Billing vs soft quota impacts: lowering global min headroom reduces cost but increases risk of customer-facing latency during multi-region correlated bursts. We should gate more aggressive min reductions behind a canary performance test.

Operational checklist for next PROD experiments: 
- Run 2-week A/B in two low-risk clusters (us-west-2-a and eu-west-1-c). Keep all customer-critical traffic on baseline.
- Instrument a new metric: util_derivative_percentile_95 over 1m windows and expose to console.
- Add alert: derivative-trigger-fire-rate > 3/min for 10m -> escalates to infra-oncall.
- Prepare rollback knob in control plane: force-min-headroom override per region.

Action items (owners):
- implement sim harness for auto-tuning derivative alpha: Alex Chen (due 2026-07-05)
- instrument derivative metrics and dashboard: Marta Lopez (due 2026-07-09)
- schedule canary A/B in low-risk clusters: Samira Patel + SRE (due 2026-07-15)
- estimate cost savings if global min headroom reduced to 10%: Ethan Brooks (finance calc, due 2026-07-07)

Notes to self (scratch):
- We saw a weird oscillation artifact when single-step limit set to 50% + derivative alpha high; likely because step brings util down then derivative reverses -> add hysteresis or increase cooldown.
- Keep a small fixed per-region slot (2 GPUs) for emergency bridging on long cold starts.

References and raw sim links:
- sim traces bucket: gs://infra-sims/jun-2026/derivative-test/*
- perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1210
- related jira: INFRA-2931, INFRA-2974 (cold-start initiatives)

Status: working draft. This sheet captures the design rationale and rough numbers; want to validate with 2-week canary before we convert to a runbook entry and create a config rollout.
